subject: [PATCH] mm/mempolicy: recompute automatic interleave weights on memory hotplug

reviews.author: David (Arm)
reviews.summary:
The reviewer, David (Arm), expressed confusion about a specific check in the code and suggested adding a comment to clarify its purpose.

Gave Acked-by
reviews.raw_body:
I was confused about the node_bw_table check at first. Maybe

/*
 * We can get hotplug events before any BW data was recorded.
 * ...
 */

reviews.author: Gregory Price (author)
reviews.summary:
Author agreed that a comment was warranted for clarity and accepted the decision to keep the mutex inside the function.

Author acknowledges that adding a warning for the -ENOMEM failure state is a reasonable suggestion and is open to making the change.
reviews.raw_body:
I went back and forth on whether to do the mutex in or outside this
function, but ultimately decided inside is just better structurally.

But yes, this comment seems warranted in this case.

---

The only failure state is -ENOMEM, wasn't sure that was worth warning
on.  I actually debated whether to just make this a void function.

I don't have a strong feeling here, but happy to add a warn if you
prefer it.

~Gregory

reviews.author: Joshua Hahn
reviews.summary:
Reviewer Joshua Hahn appreciated Gregory's patch and noted that it not only fixes the issue but also simplifies the code in mempolicy_set_node_perf() by removing nested rollbacks.

Reviewer noted that node_bw_table can be NULL at the new callsite in mempolicy_set_node_perf(), which was not expected based on initial analysis.
reviews.raw_body:
Ouch, thanks for finding this fix Gregory. In addition to making the
code correct, I think it's a nice simplification to
mempolicy_set_node_perf() since we no longer have the nested rollbacks.

---

I was also a bit confused by this because at first I thought it was a
simple code move, but this seems to be a new condition.

I traced the path in mempolicy_set_node_perf because I think 
node_bw_table must actually always be non-NULL here......

Aha! But it can indeed be NULL at the new callsite.

Thanks! This looks good to me. With or without David's suggested
pr_warn_once(), I think the change looks good to me : -) so please feel
free to add:

Reviewed-by: Joshua Hahn <joshua.hahnjy@gmail.com>

Thanks a lot Gregory, have a great day!
Joshua

2026-10-26.patch_summary: This patch updates the automatic interleave weights in Linux's memory policy when a node gains or loses memory due to hotplug events. The current implementation only recalculates the weights when a new bandwidth is reported, which can lead to incorrect weights being used for some nodes. This patch introduces a new function `wi_state_refresh` that recomputes the weights from the recorded bandwidth whenever a node gains its first memory or loses its last. This ensures that the weighted interleave algorithm always uses accurate and up-to-date weights, leading to improved performance in certain scenarios.

reviews.author: David (Arm)
reviews.summary: Reviewer David (Arm) questioned whether it's acceptable to introduce imprecision in the weighted interleave calculation, suggesting that some notification or indication of this change is necessary.
reviews.raw_body:
I'd assume we'd at least want to tell the world somehow that something is now
imprecise?

Or is not updating that harmless?

-- 
Cheers,

David

reviews.author: Gregory (Meta) (author)
reviews.summary: Author acknowledges a potential performance regression and agrees to add a warning instead of handling it as an error.
reviews.raw_body:
It's a potential performance regression, but if we just -ENOMEM'd a
kernel buffer to hold the weights, there's bigger issues.

I'll add a warn.

-- 
~Gregory
